command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: With lavfi raw input, `-c:v h264` selects an encoder path; null output is discarded and cannot be reverse decoded. This proves neither the H.264 decoder nor decoded display.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED: approve a known H.264 coded input, decoder path and measurable output/visual oracle before choosing a bounded decode command.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: H.264 Decode identity, display wording and 3/1-minute metadata remain; the suggested five-second 640x480 generator is not authoritative.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After approval, inspect and hash the H.264 input, invoke the pinned decoder/hardware API, detect fallback, retain decoded output, verify frame/timestamp/quality results and collect defined display evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Separates decoder validation from the existing encode stage and from DeepSeek's encode-to-null example.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Encoder success cannot establish bitstream parser, decode engine, reconstructed frames or scanout quality.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Malformed streams, profile/level incompatibility, software fallback, scratch growth and evidence reuse can falsely claim decode coverage.

review_improvement: Rejects encoder selection as decode proof and explicitly prevents the earlier H.264 Encode case from satisfying decoder-specific coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: H.264 decode starts with an encoded access-unit stream. DeepSeek starts with raw test frames and selects an encoder, then discards its product, so no H.264 parser or decoder processes data. A prior encoding result also cannot prove decoder reconstruction, timing or display behavior.
